E1.evidence: Public issue with reproducer code and log ("[rviz2-4] [ERROR] [1649066982.936072797] [rviz2]: Can't assign material Shape22Material to the ManualObject MeshShape_ManualObject0 because this Material does not exist in group General. Have you forgotten to define it in a .material script?"). Maintainer JafarAbdi pointed to the existing fix PR #672 (https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/issues/1164#issuecomment-1087578688); PR #672 states: "Fixes a bug causing RViz to print a ton of error messages about material not existing in the `General` resource group when adding a mesh to the planning scene". Backport PR #1165 merged to foxy (fa983f73).

E2.evidence: Step 1: MeshShape (moveit_ros/visualization/rviz_plugin_render_tools in moveit2) derives from rviz_rendering::Shape (package rviz_rendering in ros2/rviz); separately built and released packages. Step 2: the material is created by the provider's base class in its own Ogre resource group and handed to the subclass by name through the protected member material_name_: rviz_rendering 8.2.6 shape.cpp "material_name_ = entity_name + \"Material\";\n  material_ = MaterialManager::createMaterialWithLighting(material_name_);" and material_manager.cpp "Ogre::MaterialPtr material = Ogre::MaterialManager::getSingleton().create(name, \"rviz_rendering\");". The consumer references that name without a group: moveit2 517c34fb mesh_shape.cpp "manual_object_->begin(material_name_, Ogre::RenderOperation::OT_TRIANGLE_LIST);" and "entity_->setMaterialName(material_name_);". The failure depends on which group the provider registers the material in, so it is not internal. Step 3/4/5: the fix edits consumer code (adds the "rviz_rendering" group argument), not deployment names or build files.

E3.evidence: PAIR: the material created by rviz_rendering::Shape (provider output) is consumed by MeshShape when it builds the mesh for a collision object added to the planning scene ("I want to add mesh file (e.g. *.stl, *.obj, *.dae) to planning scene as collision object, but rviz2 print a lot of error messages about materials.").

E4.evidence: Observed runtime errors for each mesh: "Can't assign material Shape24Material to the ManualObject MeshShape_ManualObject1 because this Material does not exist in group General."

units.name: rviz_rendering
units.revision_basis: The reporter uses ROS Foxy installed from apt ("ROS install: apt") and reports on 2022-04-04 without an rviz version. The latest Foxy release of ros2/rviz before that date is tag 8.2.6 (9816beaa, 2022-02-04); the next, 8.2.7, is dated 2022-09-13. At 8.2.6 createMaterialWithLighting creates materials in group "rviz_rendering". The resolution changes only moveit2, so the provider keeps 8.2.6.

units.name: moveit_ros_visualization
units.revision_basis: The reporter builds moveit2 from source, "branch foxy", and reports on 2022-04-04; the foxy branch head then was 517c34fb (2022-04-01; the next foxy commit is fa983f73 on 2022-04-06). The reporter's working state is foxy with the two lines of #672 applied by hand ("I found the changes in #672 at two positions. So I changed the code at branch foxy manually. It works!"); fa983f73 (backport PR #1165) has parent 517c34fb and changes only moveit_ros/visualization/rviz_plugin_render_tools/src/mesh_shape.cpp with exactly those two lines, so it is used as the resolved revision.

failed_conditions.quote: Fixes a bug causing RViz to print a ton of error messages about material not existing in the `General` resource group when adding a mesh to the planning scene

loudness_evidence: Ogre's resource lookup refuses the material assignment and says why: "[rviz2-4] [ERROR] [1649066982.936072797] [rviz2]: Can't assign material Shape22Material to the ManualObject MeshShape_ManualObject0 because this Material does not exist in group General. Have you forgotten to define it in a .material script?" (https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/issues/1164).

resolution.summary: MeshShape passes the provider's resource group when referencing the base-class material: manual_object_->begin(material_name_, Ogre::RenderOperation::OT_TRIANGLE_LIST, "rviz_rendering") and entity_->setMaterialName(material_name_, "rviz_rendering") (moveit2 #672 on main, backported to foxy as #1165 / fa983f73).
resolution.evidence: Reporter on foxy with the two #672 lines applied to branch foxy and apt rviz: "I found the changes in #672 at two positions. So I changed the code at branch foxy manually. It works! Thank you very much!" (https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/issues/1164#issuecomment-1088609471).

notes: Class 'other': the material name itself matches; what differs is the Ogre resource group in which the provider registers it ("rviz_rendering") versus the group the consumer's unqualified reference resolves in ("General"). No fitting canonical class exists for a resource-group (namespace) qualifier; representation_convention (how the material reference is encoded across the boundary) is a possible alternative. Canonical form for the material: resource:<token> with the token being the provider's per-instance name pattern ("Shape" + count + "Material", e.g. Shape22Material in the log). Ogre (rviz_ogre_vendor) performs the group-scoped lookup and emits the error; it is a shared dependency, not one of the two units. Outcome 'failure' because the material assignment itself is refused; the source does not say how the mesh looked in RViz. The reporter first tried checking out commit 5099f70001762e5f8ec5dbde84b6f6ff3728274d (#672 on main) and reported "it doesn't work" before hand-applying the diff to foxy; that attempt used a different consumer revision and is not the resolved composition. The source gives no evidence that this composition previously worked with an earlier rviz_rendering, so it is recorded as PAIR rather than UPGRADE.
